question.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{x}2x\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A
$$

given that the region $D$ in the $xz$-plane is given by

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le z\le 2-x\}.
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{x}2x\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}2x[y]_{y=0}^{y=x}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2{x}^{2}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $D$ is a type I region in the $xz$-plane.
Therefore, to evaluate our double integral as a repeated integral over this region, we integrate with respect to $z$ and then with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2{x}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}2{x}^{2}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}2{x}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{2-x}\,\text{d}z]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}2{x}^{2}{[z]}_{z=0}^{z=2-x}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}2{x}^{2}(2-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(4{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{4}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =(\frac{32}{3}-8)-0 \\  & =\frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
